about: The look every model shares: a low-poly silhouette carried by a painted, lit texture, read from a 3/4 game camera.
rules: Light is painted into the texture as form (a sun from the upper front, a sky above, occlusion in the creases), then the colours go on top: never flat colours with noise.
Every feature is a form with a lit side and a shadow side; transitions run over 2-4 texels. No outlines anywhere, and no one-texel ring of one value round a shape.
Near-black and near-white only at the centre of small features: an eye body and its catchlight, a nostril, a mouth crease.
Each part is painted at the body's texel density (a head may be denser) and meets what it grows from at the same brightness, unless the contract marks it as a contrast: parts.density and parts.joins.
Each part keeps to its triangle budget in the contract; the parts' budgets leave the body its share of the tier: parts.budget.
Detail scales with the size on screen: a very large animal earns geometry where the camera looks (the head, the mouth), the body stays simple.
